sections.content: How many people stayed in Radstock after gaining qualifications?

Radstock is a small town in the South West. Radstock does not have its own university.

Radstock has medium levels of deprivation.

Overall, Radstock ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 485 state-school pupils from Radstock who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 120 (25%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 160 (33%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Radstock to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Radstock's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Radstock in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Radstock move to?

Of Radstock's graduates, 65 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

Of Radstock's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 70 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 45 of those qualified non-graduates (64%) were living fairly locally, in the Bath travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Radstock's GCSE cohort:

  • 35 graduates left the South West

In 2018 to 2019, 39% of graduates and 45% of qualified non-graduates living in Radstock had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 90 graduates and 155 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Radstock. This is compared with the 120 graduates and 160 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 61% of the graduates had also lived in Radstock as GCSE pupils, while 39% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Radstock in 2018 to 2019, 58% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 45% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
